title: Deep-learning design of zinc metalloproteases
summary: RFdiffusion2 for Molecular Interfaces designs zinc-dependent proteases for peptide-bond hydrolysis. The primary paper reports cleavage at the targeted bond in 36% of 135 designs and selected designs that cleave disease-associated proteins in vitro. These biochemical results do not establish therapeutic efficacy.
organization: Institute for Protein Design, University of Washington

evidence.tested: The source reports the study-specific result summarized here.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and broader deployment or clinical benefit are not established by this source review.
evidence.ai_role: RFD2-MI generates scaffolds around zinc catalytic and peptide-binding geometries; computational filtering guided experimental testing.

source_review.scope: Full primary article text, including methods and results; indexed primary full text; PDF open too large for direct retrieval
